task.title: Remove code cleanliness gates from independent Backlog authoring guidance
task.description:
## Outcome and authority
Correct the canonical and globally delivered Markdown authoring templates so an independent Backlog task store can create, revise and publish tasks without requiring its parent code repository to be clean or upstream-equal. Joe explicitly authorized this bounded documentation correction and global template delivery through ADAPT / Adapt-Hand Expert. His exact instruction was: “We need to fix the skill to make it clear there's no such requirement. We need the fix to be in the global template from prime-claw as well as our local skill file. work with Prime-Claw expert to get that into the global template, fix it locally, delete the unnecessary symlink, commit the .gitignore, create the ticket.”

Adapt-Hand Expert owns ADAPT local changes and reports them completed separately. This Prime-Claw task owns only the source/global Markdown fix. ADAPT-1 is not this work item. Completed PRIMECLAW-51 is not reopened and no terminal Episode may be borrowed. Joe has selected the behavior and replacement wording; no further product-definition approval is needed merely because this request is recorded as a task. The request includes bounded implementation, required safe validation and publication/global Markdown delivery, not a broad runtime refresh or restart. Normal lifecycle/resource admission gates remain in force.

## Confirmed defect and scope
Both src/prime-agent-plugin/skills/project-templates/design.md and spec-it-out.md, in Verify and publish exactly once → Backlog, require canonical code HEAD clean and upstream-equal even for an ignored independent ordinary-Git task store. The nearby unqualified Git-index cleanliness language is also ambiguous. Correct these equivalent authoring sections only; inspect other directly equivalent authoring guidance solely to prevent contradiction, not for a broader refactor.

The following replacement is the exact final ADAPT local block, with pre-write timing confirmed by Adapt-Hand Expert and Prime-Claw51. Use the same semantics and wording in both canonical templates:

### Backlog

Before mutation, record Git status in the code repository and the selected task
store. Require the selected existing task path and the selected task store's
Git index to be clean; do not apply task-store cleanliness checks to a separate
parent code repository. After creation or revision, reload the exact task
through `backlog task view --json -- TASK-ID` and verify its canonical ID,
`In Design` status, meaningful Description, native Acceptance Criteria, and
returned regular task path. Verify no path other than that exact returned task
path was newly changed in the task store and do not stage unrelated pre-existing
changes.

Preserve the selected store topology. If the selected Backlog store is a
validated ignored independent ordinary-Git clone, whether built-in or custom,
before the native task write require the independent clone to be clean and at
the directly proved `refs/heads/prime-claw/tasks` head. After the native task
write, verify only the exact intended task path changed, commit only that path
inside the clone, push `HEAD:refs/heads/prime-claw/tasks` without force, and prove
the direct remote head. There is no requirement for the parent code repository to be clean
or upstream-equal for task creation, revision, or task-store publication.
Unrelated staged, unstaged, or untracked code changes and code-branch divergence
are not blockers. Preserve the parent code HEAD, index, and worktree as found;
never commit, stash, reset, clean, or otherwise repair code changes to enable a
task-only operation. This does not relax separate implementation or Episode
admission requirements.
Only for an actual branch-local store, keep the existing flow: commit only the
returned task path in the code repository, prove the commit contains no other
path, and attempt one prompt push when a remote is available. A push failure is
transport evidence to report, not permission to undo the valid local
specification, create another task, or begin planning.

## Delivery and non-goals
Preserve managed asset identities and the existing native independent-store topology. Retain task/store/root identity checks, clean published independent store BEFORE its native write, exact intended task-path changes afterward, task-store index safety, scoped task-only commits, non-force push and direct-remote proof. Code noninterference is not code cleanliness; concurrent unrelated code changes are not proof this task operation modified them. Do not weaken branch-local authoring behavior or implementation/Episode admission requirements.

Validate candidate source changes only in Docker, including mandatory Tier1 probe after changes under src/prime-agent-plugin. Use focused, proportionate docs/contract regression evidence; no new validation framework. Preserve the dirty .prime-claw/templates.json and any unrelated source/index/runtime work. Report qualified test results honestly.

Publish the bounded source correction through the required normal lifecycle and deliver only the corrected global Markdown assets, using safe existing delivery surfaces if they support that scope. Prove exact destination paths and contents/hashes and absence of unrelated global/runtime changes. Do not run a broad global apply that silently refreshes other assets, do not restart, and do not invent a new delivery controller. If supported delivery cannot safely isolate these Markdown assets, report that concrete constraint rather than broadening scope or claiming global activation. Existing running processes are not claimed restarted; report actual Markdown delivery status separately from runtime activation.

No initializer/runtime/symlink-policy change, no dependency or Prime Agent changes, no live migration, no ADAPT task/source/config mutation, and no changes to completed work. The separately reported unnecessary root-symlink behavior is awareness only, outside this task.

task.title: Allow task Episodes from published non-main bases for stacked PRs
task.description:
## Observed failure

Direct report from Conversation Prime-Agent-Pi (`01a18414-077b-7038-85d3-6d13ece95269`), not a new reproduction: in `/Users/jlanders/code/prime-agent`, the owning primary checkout was clean and pushed on `fix/daemon-cwd-session-recovery`, at code HEAD/upstream `a1faacd53ac4473a75de1d434afaf50945c2f647`. This was the reviewed TypeScript baseline.

Joe invoked `/implement-task TASK-2` for “Prevent orphaned RLM settlement after child finalization errors”. Backlog was the sole valid provider, with an ignored independent ordinary-Git `.backlog` clone, origin `https://github.com/SailorJoe6/prime-agent.git`, task ref `refs/heads/prime-claw/tasks`, and task path `.backlog/tasks/task-2 - Prevent-orphaned-RLM-settlement-after-child-finalization-errors.md`. The task was `In Planning`, with a meaningful 642-word plan, seven unchecked acceptance criteria and no blocking dependencies. Its complete specification/plan had been read and judged ready; task HEAD, FETCH_HEAD and direct published revision agreed at `61b5bfe5870e2d04ff092d6280db894f104c1997`.

The canonical readiness workflow completed preparation and called `create_task_episode` exactly once with `{"taskId":"TASK-2"}`. It returned:

> Task Episode creation failed: Task-native Episode creation must run from the canonical primary main checkout

Afterward, the task remained field-for-field unchanged in `In Planning`; the task clone remained clean and published at the same revision; no `.prime-claw/ownership.json` existed; and the worktree inventory contained only the original primary and existing cwd-fix/upstream-assessment trees, with no new Episode tree. Code stayed clean and unchanged. No implementation, status change, assignment/handoff, branch switch, bypass or creation retry was attempted. These are observed native/Git/filesystem facts, not proof about unseen resources.

Local main was `08ff1b2e2794ea9e8f4a08d12bc95408a66e1074` (v0.9.7), four commits behind the selected baseline (`main...HEAD` = `0/4`); origin/main was independently newer/different. Switching to main would change the approved implementation basis. No switch, merge, pull or reset workaround was authorized.

Joe's feedback: '"The tool requires the canonical primary main checkout" bad design. it blocks stacking PRs and other such fun'

## Source evidence and diagnosis

Prime Claw source inspected at `24b519c3c967269dd3867bf06a9e92a2f125012d`: `src/prime-agent-plugin/extension-support/spec-episode.ts:3145-3153` rejects `git.branch(projectRoot) !== "main"` alongside primary-checkout identity checks. Beads admission repeats this at `2913-2921`. This confirms a literal branch-name restriction; equating primary ownership with main is the inferred design defect, not a newly reproduced runtime trace.

Downstream assumptions also need coherent treatment: task blocked handling (`977-984`), handoff (`1776-1782`), cleanup (`2671-2673`), and terminal publication/ancestry checks (`2547-2605`, including Beads direct-remote `main`). Managed oversight at `src/prime-agent-plugin/skills/prime-claw-oversee-episode/SKILL.md:41-49` hardcodes main for readiness, merge and abandonment. `src/prime-agent-plugin/workflows/implement-task.md:90` also assumes canonical main. Removing only the admission check is insufficient.

## Intended outcome and boundaries

Use the current checked-out branch as the Episode base and default merge target, including a clean, published feature/stack branch in the primary owning checkout. Show its name and exact base commit during readiness; bind that commit and integration branch so continuation, review, merge and cleanup use the correct target. The repository's actual primary/default branch is supported regardless of whether it is named main, master or something else; it is not a universal admission gate. Preserve task/provider/publication/owner/resource identity, isolated Episode resources, and explicit operator merge/abandonment authority.

The implement-task skill must instruct the LLM to check whether the current branch differs from the repository's actual primary/default branch. If it does, the LLM should ask the user before stacking, for example: "Current branch is xxxx; are you sure you want to stack a branch off this?" This is ONLY an instruction in the skill file. Add no code to require, track, validate or enforce this check-in, no approval token/receipt, and no deterministic confirmation gate or compliance test. Joe explicitly accepts that the LLM may ignore this instruction. This does not weaken the separate existing identity, isolation or publication checks.

Use native Git/provider behavior and the smallest explicit binding needed. Do not introduce a branch classifier, reconciler, coordinator, new state machine or lifecycle receipts. This bug concerns task-native admission and affected downstream target assumptions, not blanket permission for arbitrary checkout admission. Preserve legacy compatibility and the distinct post-acceptance primary-main `--user-global` activation policy. No Prime Agent source changes, release/Rust/fork proposals, or changes to foreign TASK-2 are in scope. This ticket authorizes specification review only, not planning, implementation or real Episode reproduction.

nodes.title: Allow task Episodes from published non-main bases for stacked PRs

acceptanceCriteria.text: The current checked-out branch is the Episode base and default merge target. A clean, published non-default branch in the primary owning checkout can admit an otherwise-ready task Episode without changing that baseline; the repository default branch is supported regardless of its name.

The exact base commit and intended integration branch remain unambiguous for the same owner/task/Episode through continuation, blocked handling, review and terminal cleanup; merge and publication target that integration branch rather than a hardcoded main.

Admission never silently switches the primary checkout to main, discards stacked commits or substitutes another implementation basis. Existing unsafe-state, provider/publication, owner and resource identity rejections remain effective, with isolation preserved.

Merge and abandonment still require explicit operator authority. Task status/publication and terminal ancestry checks remain correct for the selected target; unrelated tasks and resources are not changed.

Focused disposable regression evidence covers clean published non-main acceptance with isolation/identity and invalid admission leaving task/resources unchanged. Review affected managed instructions for consistent target handling; do not require a new broad test harness or matrix.
The change stays within Prime Claw, preserves legacy compatibility and does not loosen the separate primary-main user-global activation policy or introduce unnecessary coordination/state machinery.

Content review confirms the implement-task skill tells the LLM to ask the user before stacking from a branch other than the repository’s actual primary/default branch, naming the current branch. This check-in exists only as a skill instruction: no code enforcement, confirmation tracking/receipt or compliance test is added; LLM noncompliance is explicitly acceptable.

task.implementationPlan:
## Scope and implementation basis

Implement only PRIMECLAW-48 in Prime Claw. The current checked-out branch is the code base and default integration target; show the branch and exact SHA during readiness. Keep the owning primary-root requirement, provider-native publication and unsafe-state/resource checks. This plan does not authorize implementation, real Episode reproduction, foreign TASK-2 changes or user-global activation.

Current source at `fe61016a5eab4a41f7d10fe3ca3996d3bb0d3fc8` confirms literal-main restrictions in `extension-support/spec-episode.ts` admission, task blocked handling, handoff and finalization. Existing ownership has `baseRef` and the Episode `branch`, but no integration target. Use these existing boundaries rather than adding orchestration.

## Ordered work

1. **Put the stacking check-in only in the skill.** Update `src/prime-agent-plugin/skills/implement-task/SKILL.md` to have the LLM inspect the current branch and the repository's actual primary/default branch using ordinary Git evidence (not a literal `main` assumption). On a non-default branch, instruct it to ask: “Current branch is xxxx; are you sure you want to stack a branch off this?” Show current branch and code SHA during readiness. Add no confirmation argument, code enforcement, approval token/receipt, tracking or compliance test. LLM failure to ask is explicitly acceptable. This must not become a second readiness/approval mechanism.

2. **Bind the integration branch in existing task ownership.** Add one task-only `integrationBranch` field to the version-2 types/allowlists/parser in `extension-support/episode-ownership.ts`, and carry it through the three reservation inputs/factories in `extension-support/task-episode-ownership.ts`. Fresh admissions always record the current named branch; `baseRef` continues to identify the exact code base and `branch` continues to identify the isolated Episode branch. Use ordinary Git branch/ref validation. Include the effective target in existing `sameEpisodeBinding` immutability checks so an active owner cannot silently retarget. Old version-2 records without the field retain their previous `main` target through one narrow compatibility fallback; never infer their target from whichever branch is now checked out. Leave version-1 records and their main-only transition/activation policy unchanged. Preserve this field across provider migration and same-owner evidence/routing updates; do not migrate or rewrite live ownership. No new schema generation, state machine, target registry or receipt.

3. **Admit from that branch without changing the baseline.** In Backlog `createTaskEpisode` and Beads `createBeadsTaskEpisode` in `extension-support/spec-episode.ts`, replace only the task-native literal-main gate with capture/validation of the current named branch. Retain repository-root/primary-worktree, persisted top-level owner, placement, exact task status/plan, and nonterminal ownership checks. Recheck branch and code identity at the existing serialized/publication/reservation boundaries so a switch cannot silently retarget admission. Independent Backlog and Beads keep code and provider DAGs separate and retain their clean published-code proofs against the selected branch's configured upstream. Grandfathered branch-local Backlog retains its exact task-only status commit as `baseRef` and existing prompt-push behavior. Pass the target to the reservation before any resource allocation; provision the worktree from the exact `baseRef`, never by switching the primary checkout or substituting default-branch HEAD. Preserve existing rollback/Blocked/no-retry behavior and one fixed execute assignment.

4. **Use the same target for the rest of the task lifecycle.** Update task-native blocked handling, `handoffTaskEpisode`, `allocateReservedTaskEpisode` fresh/replay branch identity checks, and `finalizeTaskEpisodeCleanup`/`verifyTaskEpisodeTerminalState` in `spec-episode.ts` to use the recorded integration target instead of `main`. The owner checkout must match that branch; if it has switched, report the mismatch without switching, rebinding or allocating again. Normal target-branch advancement remains allowed under existing ancestry/publication rules; do not pin its HEAD forever to admission. Fresh review/merge evidence names the integration branch plus target and candidate heads. Check pushed terminal code and merged/abandoned Episode ancestry against that target, including Beads direct-remote checks; keep independent Backlog terminal evidence on its task ref. Preserve exact owner/task/provider/resources, idle-work checks and cleanup-only behavior. Cleanup still deletes only the Episode’s own configured upstream, never the integration branch. Keep explicit operator merge/abandonment authority; do not add retarget automation or a coordinator.

5. **Align managed instructions and focused docs.** Update the task-native portions of `workflows/implement-task.md`, `skills/prime-claw-oversee-episode/SKILL.md`, relevant execute/blocked/handoff/expert guidance, and the `finalize_task_episode` tool description in `extensions/reviewed-plan.ts` so readiness, review, status publication, merge and cleanup name the recorded integration target. Update `docs/conversation-driven-episode-oversight.md` and affected promotion/finalization user stories/traceability. Review each main reference rather than globally replacing it: retained version-1 workflows, legacy bridge and accepted-primary-main `--user-global` refresh/restart/UAT rules stay unchanged. Change inert source assets, not the installed global skill/plugin; no host apply/check/probe.

6. **Prove the change with existing disposable suites.** Extend `tests/task_episode_admission_extension.test.mjs` and `tests/beads_task_episode_admission_extension.test.mjs`: accept a clean published feature/stack base without losing its commits, retain the exact base/target through one isolated allocation, support a default branch named `master` or another non-main name, and replace the obsolete “primary non-main rejects” assertion while retaining linked-worktree rejection. Add focused pre-mutation detached/unsafe or branch-drift rejection assertions with unchanged task/ownership/resources. Extend existing ownership/handoff/blocked/close cases to show target retention, normal same-branch advancement, rejection of wrong-target cleanup, and correct merged/abandoned terminal ancestry/publication on the feature target. Retain old version-2 missing-target, provider-switch field preservation, forbidden active-target mutation and version-1 compatibility coverage and local/Orca identity coverage without creating a broad cross-product matrix. Review skill wording as content; add no test of whether the LLM asked or the user confirmed.

Run affected Node behavior suites only through their existing Docker Tier-1 pytest bridges (`tests/test_task_providers.py`, `tests/test_reviewed_plan_extension.py`), plus relevant policy/docs checks. After every plugin-source change run the required Tier-1 validation, such as `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe` or `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -m container`. Record actual results and any blockers in the native task during the later implementation Episode; do not claim tests have run during planning. Keep documentation and acceptance evidence current, commit/push the reviewed implementation candidate, then return it to the owning Conversation for review. Merge, abandonment, activation/restart and cleanup remain separate lifecycle decisions, not consequences of this plan.

task.title: Migrate prime-claw to Backlog.md v1.55.3
task.description:
Backlog.md v1.55.3 is upstream’s current stable release, verified by agreement between the non-prerelease GitHub release and npm `latest` at exact upstream commit `0cf4fdbc70020327f4366a29d3f405f83d180301`. Prime-claw remains built and documented against v1.53.0, and a read-only compatibility review found that advancing the dependency without adapting prime-claw would break provider migration and make task-history evidence inaccurate.

The migration must align prime-claw’s supported CLI/MCP behavior, provider-history conversion, shipped agent guidance, fixtures, distribution pins, and provenance with the v1.55.3 lifecycle. In that lifecycle, a task becomes closed by reaching the configured final status while remaining active; archive is a reversible, read-only off-board state that preserves identity, status, dependencies, and references; restore returns it to the board; delete is the explicit archived-only identity-vacating operation. Legacy `completed/` and canonical `archive/tasks/` records are both archived corpus members until `doctor --fix` migrates legacy storage.

The historical reversal and migration mapping are explicit:

| v1.53 source state or intent | v1.55.3 representation |
| --- | --- |
| Active task in a non-final status | Open active task in the same non-final status |
| Active task in the configured final status | Closed active task in that final status |
| Record stored under legacy `completed/` | Archived record preserving its final status and history |
| Record stored under `archive/tasks/`, including an old cancellation or soft deletion | Archived record preserving its status and history; migration never silently deletes it |
| Future operator intent to permanently discard a record, clean relationships, and vacate its identity | Explicit archive followed by archived-only `task delete` |

Thus the old archive command’s destructive identity-cleanup meaning moves to explicit `delete` for future operations, while pre-existing archived and completed records are preserved during migration. “Closed” remains a status-derived classification, not a storage directory or a replacement native status.

Current incompatibilities include the removed `backlog task complete` call in provider migration, classification of legacy completed records as closed instead of archived, and migration evidence that temporarily relocates archived files into active directories before native viewing. Public docs, installed skills, templates, and tests also teach the obsolete completion flow and old storage path, while build/runtime/submodule/provenance surfaces remain pinned to v1.53.0.

Scope includes the complete prime-claw compatibility change and the managed Backlog candidate/version advance needed to ship it. Preserve the existing single-provider, exact-history, source-authoritative migration guarantees and the Docker-only plugin validation boundary. Do not patch Prime Agent, modify upstream Backlog.md source, move the Backlog.md Expert repository’s separate `latest-stable` branch, weaken migration proof, or introduce a compatibility shim for the removed completion command. Ordering and pagination need only remain correct for prime-claw’s actual identity-set reads; interactive `cleanup` is not part of prime-claw’s workflow.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every managed Backlog build, runtime image, submodule/provenance record, fixture, and version assertion consistently identifies a reviewed v1.55.3-compatible candidate whose history contains upstream tag commit `0cf4fdbc70020327f4366a29d3f405f83d180301`.

No prime-claw runtime path or shipped instruction treats `backlog task complete` or MCP `task_complete` as available; a migrated closed source task becomes an active task in the configured final status, while only an archived source record becomes archived.

Provider inspection, conversion counts, destination state, and receipts classify both legacy `completed/` records and canonical `archive/tasks/` records as archived, and classify closed only from active tasks in the configured final status.

Exact source and destination evidence for archived tasks is captured through the native archived-task read surface without moving, copying, or presenting the record as active, including coverage for both legacy and canonical archive storage.

Shipped documentation, customizable skills, canonical templates, and their installed mirrors consistently describe final-status edit followed by archive, restore-before-edit, archived-only permanent delete, and `archive/tasks/`; `completed/` appears only as legacy migration input.

Migration and lifecycle tests prove identity, status, dependency, parent, documentation, and reference preservation across archive/restore and truthful identity cleanup on delete, including archived tasks whose status is and is not the configured final status.

Prime-claw’s task-list consumers remain correct under v1.55.3 default ordering and pagination semantics without depending on implicit row position, and fully specified noninteractive initialization remains successful.

The candidate passes the repository’s required migration/lifecycle suites, Tier 0 and Tier 1 Docker validation, Git certificate/private-proxy smoke coverage, and Nix task persistence/build smoke coverage.
Failure at any compatibility, provenance, build, or validation gate leaves the currently accepted v1.53.0 artifact authoritative and does not activate or publish a partial v1.55.3 upgrade.

task.implementationPlan:
## Approved scope and specification clarifications

Implement the complete prime-claw compatibility change against Backlog.md v1.55.3, exact upstream tag commit `0cf4fdbc70020327f4366a29d3f405f83d180301`. The following operator decisions supersede the conflicting PRIMECLAW-44 policy and clarify the acceptance criteria:

- Archive retains/reserves identity; only explicit archived-only delete vacates it. Both `completed/` and `archive/tasks/` are archived history, not active closed tasks.
- Existing duplicate IDs, including archive/live collisions formerly allowed by PRIMECLAW-44, refuse before cutover. Report exact conflicts and preserve source and destination baseline unchanged. Repair, renumbering, and automatic `doctor --fix` are outside this task.
- A successful merged Episode remains active `Done` through `finalize_task_episode`; optional archive comes afterward. AC5 does not require immediate archive or an archived-Done finalizer extension. Preserve archived non-Done abandonment plus its exact Final Summary contract.
- Beads imports map source status normally (`closed` -> `Done`), then archive only from explicit source archive/abandonment evidence. Preserve raw source status, closure reason, and abandonment provenance; do not force archived imports to `In Progress` or infer a lost pre-close status.
- Adopt native v1.55.3 dependency eligibility, including archived and draft targets. Retire PRIMECLAW-44's custom exclusions rather than porting its downstream patches.

No Prime Agent or Backlog source changes, removed-command shim, reverse-migration revival, interactive cleanup, new provider framework, reconciliation state machine, semantic classifier, or persistent approval/checkpoint store. Do not implement deterministic task reconciliation, iterative plan revision, or semantic compatibility decisions. Episode and Conversation LLMs own that reasoning; code enforces only concrete identity, integrity, and transport constraints. Add only narrow native read/identity/transport adaptations required below. The implementation candidate must not move the Backlog Expert's separate `latest-stable` branch or activate a host/global artifact.

## Implementation slices

### 1. Establish the exact release and reproducible candidate (AC1, AC9)

In the isolated implementation workspace, retrieve and verify upstream `refs/tags/v1.55.3` resolves to the exact commit above; pin `deps/backlog` to that unmodified source. Do not replay the three v1.53.0 downstream restore/dependency patches: their policy is superseded. Current local `431e95612d6167e418c507ec206d95df43c38c54` and accepted host artifact remain the fallback, not the new source.

The target object is currently absent locally and the managed fork exposes no v1.55.3 tag. Use the verified upstream repository for this unmodified release and align the submodule URL plus any Docker fetch source; do not assume the fork exposes the object or move/publish an Expert branch. Update `scripts/build-backlog.sh`, `docker/runtime.Dockerfile`, both build/runtime ARG sets in `docker/test.Dockerfile`, `tests/test_backlog_build.py`, runtime source-identity assertions, build stamps/labels, and current provenance together. Require exact HEAD and exact release-tag resolution/ancestry, frozen install, version stamping, standalone compilation, and upstream compiled-binary smoke. Replace the obsolete fixed four-commit fetch expectation with the correct exact release fetch. Use upstream's documented/CI-selected Bun `1.4.4` for the isolated Backlog build/tests, updating the Backlog builder pins and matching assertions rather than assuming existing `1.3.11` compatibility. Keep other dependency/runtime versions unchanged unless an actual compatibility defect requires review; in particular, do not upgrade Prime Agent's Node runtime. Only if changes to the corresponding tooling integration require upstream build-security/updater regressions, use isolated Node `26.12.1` or later and upstream-selected npm `12.2.1` for those tests. Do not require extra Node/npm tooling solely to consume the compiled Backlog release. These are supported-tool selections, not package `engines` requirements.
